verdict_reason: The isolation core is sound and well-tested with fakes, but `--diff` on the http engine asks a reviewer to read a patch its pack cannot carry (a consultation record whose premise is false), and one claimed invariant (writes watched "gitignored or not") is not true; both are cheap fixes.
reply_markdown:
**Q1. Same revision.** Sound. `--rev` resolves once to a full sha via `rev-parse --verify <rev>^{commit}` (`crates/c3/src/engines/worktree.rs:46`), which refuses blobs/trees and leading dashes (`rev_token_ok`, `crates/c3/src/consult/reviewed.rs:89`); the worktree is added at the resolved sha (`worktree.rs:95`), so a branch moving between resolve and checkout cannot split a run. A panel resolves once and hands every member the full sha (`crates/c3/src/panel/run.rs:813`, `member.rs:244`), so members cannot diverge. Ambiguous names are resolved by git once; the recorded sha is what is checked out. Shallow clones work for any sha git knows; others are refused before anything starts. Findings do stay bound to live HEAD under `--rev` (ledger `base_commit` from the live tree; `worktree.sha` disambiguates) — as claimed; a reader of `base_commit` alone could mis-apply, but the record is truthful.

**Q2. Staging.** Copies the task's `handoffs/` (minus `*.events.jsonl`), `state.md`, and the brief (`reviewed.rs:290-325`). Destination safety is real: `stageable_rel` refuses `..`/absolute (`worktree.rs:482`), `real_parent_inside` requires every component to be a real directory and canonicalizes inside the root (`worktree.rs:206`), a destination that is a link is refused (`worktree.rs:154`) — F11-3's overwrite-through-link is closed. It can overwrite the worktree's tracked copy of the brief (intended). Two read-side notes: a live `handoffs` that is itself a symlink is followed (`is_dir`, `reviewed.rs:299`) and content from outside the repo is staged in; and any untracked file in handoffs is staged by design. Event streams are excluded.

**Q3. `--diff` and its index.** The temp-index path is clean: the real index is only read (`fs::copy`), `GIT_INDEX_FILE` points `ls-files`/`add --intent-to-add`/`diff` at the temp copy, and the unit test byte-compares the real index and confirms the new file stays untracked (`reviewed.rs:880-901`); a concurrent commit only changes a snapshot. Option injection is refused (leading `-`, whitespace; `parse_diff_spec`, `reviewed.rs:416`). Two gaps: the patch carries full contents of every untracked, not-ignored file (`reviewed.rs:639`) — a not-ignored secret lands in handoffs and the prompt (finding #6); and the patch path is shared by brief stem, so a later run or member with different bytes replaces the file an earlier ledger `diff.sha256` binds (finding #3).

**Q4. Cleanup.** Removal is Drop-based on every in-process path including the setup failure (`worktree.rs:244`, `mod.rs:4085`); kill/crash leaves the `c3-kimi-wt-<32hex>` directory with its owner record for `c3 branches`/`doctor --fix` — which still rests on the fail-open liveness and best-effort owner write of F12-1/F13-8, now covering far more worktrees. The removal itself never follows a link and aborts destructiveness on any error (`worktree.rs:290-317`).

**Q5. Classification and races.** Correctly re-scoped: live tree/collab/brief/artifact changes are warnings only (`tree.rs:191-276`), the worktree's own changes decide (`tree.rs:279`, snapshot taken after staging, `reviewed.rs:326`), and a live-tree change no longer skips the timeout continuation (`secondary.rs:399`). kimi fails on its own worktree write, claude/grok/muse warn, codex fails — consistent with prior semantics. Gap: writes to gitignored paths are invisible (`revision.rs:314`), so kimi's fail-on-write and the "gitignored or not" claim overstate (finding #4). Names are uuids — no collisions; Windows reparse points count as links in staging, checking and removal alike.

**Q6. Privacy and entry points.** http+`--rev` warns; http+`--diff` does not, and the http pack holds only brief+artifacts (`http.rs:186`), so its prompt names a patch it cannot read — finding #1. The uncommitted-path list puts up to 20 live-tree filenames, unescaped, into prompts sent to remote models (finding #5, supersedes F11-5). MCP `rev`/`diff` are validated (syntax in `args.rs:645`, existence in `build_context`) before any git call. No new child-mark concerns. CHANGELOG sentences match the code except through finding #4's doc claim.

**Q7. Untested.** Everything against a real reviewer CLI (per the brief); http+`--diff` end to end; the ignored-write escape; concurrent members sharing one patch name; autocrlf fidelity of patch bytes; `doctor --fix` on rev/frozen-head leftovers.

## Requested checks
- RC1 (finding #1): with a stub endpoint logging request bodies, run `c3 consult --engine http --purpose diff-review --diff HEAD --brief <md> --artifact <f>` in a scratch repo (workspace-write for the stub); observe whether the prompt names a patch absent from the pack. 10 min.
- RC2 (finding #4): scratch repo with `ignored.txt` gitignored; fake-kimi consult writing only `ignored.txt` in its worktree; read `tree_check_outcome`. 10 min.
- RC3 (finding #3): 2-member panel with `--diff HEAD`, touch a tracked file between member starts; compare each member's ledger `diff.sha256` with the on-disk patch. 15 min.
- RC4 (finding #2): hold `.git/index.lock` in a scratch repo and run a kimi consult; also compare `.git/index` mtime before/after worktree creation. 10 min.

findings.claim: `--diff` on the http engine writes a patch and adds "read it first and review that change" to the prompt, but the http reviewer receives only a pack built from the brief and bound artifacts, so it is asked to review a change it cannot see; unlike `--rev`+http there is no warning.

evidence.observation: build_pack's doc and body: the pack is built from the brief and -Artifact files only; a grep of http.rs finds no handling of `diff`.
diff_plan/diff_line are built for every engine; only `--rev` has an http-engine warning branch.
diff_prompt_line instructs the reviewer to read the patch file first.

findings.verification: RC1: run http+--diff against a stub endpoint and inspect the prompt vs the pack.
findings.remedy: Refuse or warn for http+--diff (mirroring the --rev warning), or include the patch bytes in the pack.

findings.claim: ThrowawayWorktree::create runs `git status --porcelain` in the live repository without `--no-optional-locks`, so every kimi run, claude diff-review/acceptance and `--rev` run can refresh (write) the live index and contend for index.lock — the discipline F04-1 established for the read-only commands is missing on this new hot path.
findings.trigger: A consult while another git process holds or creates index.lock, or with a stale index stat cache.
findings.verification: RC4: hold .git/index.lock and run a kimi consult; check .git/index mtime after creation.
findings.remedy: Add `--no-optional-locks` to the status call (or derive main_dirty from uncommitted_paths).

findings.claim: The patch file name is derived from the brief's stem and is shared across runs and panel members; write_patch overwrites the file whenever its bytes differ, so a later run (or a sibling member rendering `--diff HEAD` at a different moment) silently replaces the bytes an earlier ledger `diff {sha256}` record binds.
findings.trigger: Two consultations on one brief with different --diff values, or a panel with `--diff HEAD` while the working tree changes between members' renders.

evidence.observation: patch_name reuses the brief stem whenever the brief sits in the task's handoffs.
write_patch overwrites plan.path unless the on-disk sha already matches.
every member of a panel receives the same --diff value, so members share the path.

findings.verification: RC3: 2-member panel with --diff HEAD and a tree edit between member starts; compare ledger sha256 with the file.
findings.remedy: Make the name unique per range/content (or refuse to clobber a file whose bytes differ from what a ledger record binds).

findings.claim: ReviewTree::changes() cannot see writes to gitignored paths (git status and the content map exclude ignored files), so a kimi reviewer that writes only inside an ignored path stays usable, while the code doc and the handoff invariant claim coverage "gitignored or not".
findings.trigger: A kimi (or codex) reviewer writes inside a gitignored directory of its throwaway worktree.

evidence.observation: the fingerprint uses `git status --porcelain=v1 -uall -z` without --ignored, so ignored paths never appear.
the note literally says "ignored files excluded".
the doc comment of changes() claims "tracked and untracked files of the checkout ... gitignored or not".

findings.verification: RC2: fake-kimi consult writing only a gitignored file; read tree_check_outcome.
findings.remedy: Include ignored files in the worktree-side compare (e.g. a directory walk) or correct the claim.

findings.claim: The isolation paragraph lists up to 20 uncommitted live-tree paths (plus a count of the rest) in every worktree-isolated reviewer's prompt — now claude diff-review/acceptance and every `--rev` engine, not only kimi — with filenames passed through unescaped (Markdown delimiters, line breaks), sending private or adversarial names to remote models.
findings.trigger: Any isolated run on a repository with uncommitted files whose names are confidential or crafted for prompt injection.

evidence.observation: uncommitted_paths/isolation_prompt_line list the whole tree's status paths, take(20), wrapped in backticks only.
the match on isolation applies isolation_prompt to every non-rev isolated run.

findings.verification: Capture a fake claude diff-review prompt with a sensitive untracked filename outside the reviewed path.
findings.remedy: Restrict the list to the -Range/-Artifact focus, escape names, or make the listing opt-in.

findings.claim: A one-revision `--diff` includes the full contents of every untracked, not-ignored file, so a secret not covered by .gitignore is copied into the task's handoffs and handed to the reviewer model.
findings.trigger: `--diff HEAD` (or any single revision) with an untracked secret file in the tree.

evidence.observation: ls-files --others --exclude-standard feeds intent-to-add into the diff, so untracked non-ignored files' contents enter the patch.

findings.verification: Create an untracked secrets.txt and run --diff HEAD; inspect the patch bytes.
findings.remedy: Document the exposure or exclude dotfile/secret-looking names by default.
